accident_report:
Vehicles V1, V2, V3, and V4 are traveling on a one-way three-lane roadway with a gentle left-hand curve on flat terrain. V1 is in lane 2, positioned furthest ahead, moving at 70 km/h with steady throttle, intending to maintain lane through the curve. V2 follows V1 in the same lane at a distance of approximately 25 meters, traveling at 68 km/h, maintaining what appears to be a safe following distance under normal conditions. V3 is in lane 3 (rightmost lane), slightly behind V2 by 10 meters, traveling at 65 km/h, intending to continue straight without lane changes. V4 is in lane 1 (leftmost lane), roughly parallel to V2 but 5 meters behind, traveling at 72 km/h, intending to gradually overtake traffic. The road surface is wet due to ongoing heavy rain, and visibility is reduced by adverse weather. A continuous rigid guardrail is present along the outer edge of lane 3 following the curve.

As the vehicles enter the curved segment, the wet and slippery road surface reduces tire-road friction. V1 slightly reduces speed from 70 km/h to 62 km/h to maintain stability on the curve, causing V2 to perceive a need for coordinated speed adjustment. V2 begins moderate braking, reducing speed from 68 km/h to 60 km/h, maintaining its following distance. However, due to reduced visibility from rain, V3 does not immediately detect V2’s deceleration and continues at 65 km/h until the gap closes to approximately 8 meters. V3 then performs a sudden emergency braking maneuver, attempting to reduce speed rapidly. Because of the slippery surface, V3’s deceleration is less effective, and its speed only drops to 58 km/h while the vehicle begins to exhibit slight longitudinal instability.

Simultaneously, V4 in lane 1 observes V2’s deceleration and attempts to maintain speed coordination by reducing speed from 72 km/h to 64 km/h. However, V4 misjudges the curvature and lateral grip, drifting slightly toward lane 2 due to reduced traction. This lateral drift causes V2 to react defensively: V2 increases braking intensity to avoid a potential side conflict, dropping further to 52 km/h. This stronger deceleration propagates backward. V3, already in emergency braking on a low-friction surface, cannot generate sufficient braking force and closes the remaining gap quickly.

The situation escalates as V3 attempts to steer slightly right to avoid V2, but the presence of the rigid guardrail along lane 3 prevents lateral escape. The combined effects of wet pavement, emergency braking, and limited maneuvering space result in V3 failing to avoid V2.

The first collision occurs when V3 rear-ends V2 at approximately 55 km/h relative speed difference reduced to about 3 km/h at impact. The collision involves V2 and V3 only, triggered by the chain of coordinated deceleration, reduced visibility, slippery conditions, and constrained lateral space due to the guardrail.
